sections.h2: How to reach the Stokes County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Walk in at 1014 Main Street, Danbury, ZIP 27016, or write to P.O. Box 67. The office line is (336) 593-2414 and the fax is (336) 593-9360.

Stokes County Register of Deeds service windows
ServiceWeekday hours
General office8:30 to 5:00
Recording documents8:30 to 4:45
Marriage license applicationsUntil 4:30

The recording window closes a quarter hour before the office does, so a deed delivered at ten to five likely waits until the next business day.

sections.h2: What this office does in a home sale
sections.html:
This office keeps, indexes and preserves land and vital records for the county. A typical sale produces three filings: the seller's deed, a deed of trust for the buyer's loan if there is one, and a release of the seller's old loan.

Stokes County was split off in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry County, so a title chain for land near the line may run into Surry's books, which go back to 1771.

sections.h2: Does a Stokes County deed need tax clearance first?
sections.html:
It does. Tax Administration requires that every deed offered for recording include its certification that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property being transferred (G.S. 161-31).

An unpaid bill therefore holds the deed back. The tax office shares the building and street address, so the errand is short, and it keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00. Ask for the current-year balance at the same visit, so you know what the closing attorney must pay from your proceeds before the register takes the deed.

The statute fixes the prices. A standard instrument is $26.00 for its first 15 pages, then $4.00 per page after that. Mortgages and deeds of trust begin at $64.00 and cover 35 pages. Recording a loan release is free.

A document that breaks the formatting rules adds $25.00, and each extra instrument in one filing adds $10.00. No other fees apply, and payment comes before filing. The seller's deed tax is a separate charge, also paid at this counter.

sections.h2: Why fast filing helps both sides
sections.html:
North Carolina ranks competing claims by the order of registration. Until a deed is registered where the property sits, it does not defeat lien creditors or paying buyers (G.S. 47-18).

The buyer wants priority. The seller wants a clean break, because claims against the buyer that arise afterward cannot reach back. Keep a copy showing the date and time of filing. If a late afternoon closing runs past 4:45, ask your attorney whether the deed can be filed first thing the next business day, and make sure no new liens or judgments are likely to land in the gap.

Yes, record them. Chapter 47H covers sales where the seller keeps title to a home of up to four units and the buyer makes at least five installments. The contract itself, or a memorandum of it, goes on file within five business days of signing, and the buyer may cancel until midnight on the third business day.

  • A default notice must leave a cure period of at least 30 days.
  • Late charges stop at 4% and start only after 15 days.

If you sold this way years ago, check that the memorandum is indexed in Danbury.

sections.h2: What a seller can do before recording day
sections.html:
Go over this list with your closing attorney.

  • Verify the parcel on the county GIS site and the property record card.
  • Pick up the tax certification from the office down the hall.
  • Figure the deed tax from the sale price at $1.00 per $500.00.
  • Make sure an old mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Arrive before 4:45 on a weekday.

For title questions about an inherited or vacant house, speak with a North Carolina attorney, and call the register about document form.

Small estates can skip full administration. An heir can wait 30 days and then file an affidavit with the superior court clerk in the decedent's home county, if personal property net of liens is under $20,000 (under $30,000 when a surviving spouse is the only heir). Every tract of land the person owned must be described in it.

Larger estates take the longer route. Either way, the deed that finally conveys the house is filed in Danbury with the tax certification, so bring the court papers.

sections.h2: What happens to a recorded deed of trust in a foreclosure?
sections.html:
A lender or trustee starts by filing a notice of hearing with the clerk of superior court. The clerk has to find a valid debt, a default and a right to foreclose. An owner can appeal that finding in 10 days by posting a bond of 1% of principal unless the judge lowers it.

After the sale is reported, upset bids must top the last one by 5% or $750 added, whichever is greater, with a deposit. A borrower who sells before the hearing usually keeps more equity, and the payoff ends with a release filed in Danbury.

sections.h2: The tax calendar and your deed
sections.html:
Stokes bills come due by January 5, with interest from January 6. The tax certification a deed needs reflects what the county's books show owed on the parcel at that moment, so a house sold in autumn, after bills go out, usually has an open current-year balance.

Plan to settle it at the closing table. Tax Administration can quote a figure, and the tax website lists property record cards and land and home values that confirm what the county has on file for your parcel.

sections.h2: Other offices at the Danbury address
sections.html:
The Administration Building at 1014 Main Street houses more than one office a seller will visit. Tax Administration is there, along with Planning and Inspections at (336) 593-2444, and the Finance Department, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 20.

  • Planning and Inspections keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and asks that permit applications arrive by 4:30 in the afternoon to be processed the same day.
  • The Finance Department takes calls at (336) 914-9188.
  • The Register of Deeds answers at (336) 593-2414.

One trip to Danbury can therefore cover the tax certification, a permit question and the recording itself.

Do the errands in this order. Tax Administration comes first, because the certification must be in hand and any balance settled. Then go to the register with the signed deed, the filing fee and the deed tax payment, and ask for the stamp showing date and time. Hold on to the receipt.

A paid-off lender's release costs nothing to file, yet someone has to file it, so ask who will. The location of the house in the county affects permits and utilities, but every deed records in Danbury. Check the parcel on the county GIS site before you advertise the property, and keep the book and page reference once the deed is indexed.

faqs.q: What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds recording hours?
faqs.a: Recording runs from 8:30 to 4:45 on weekdays, with the general office open 8:30 to 5:00.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Stokes County deeds?
faqs.a: P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

faqs.q: Does a Stokes deed need tax clearance first?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property before the deed is offered for recording.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax in Danbury?
faqs.a: The seller pays at the register's window ahead of recording. The rate is one dollar for every $500.00 of price, and a leftover amount counts as another block.

faqs.q: Is a loan release free to record in Danbury?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no fee for filing a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.
